title: 926 Steps, Two Lobotomies, and Zero Nudges: Flight-Testing the Commitment Machine Across Gemini, Claude, and GPT-OSS
why_read: An eccentric, jargon-heavy personal narrative about using AI coding agents in production, likely light on rigorous technical detail despite dramatic framing.
analysis: This post describes the author's experience applying a custom workflow ('Commitment Machine') to manage AI coding agents like Gemini, Claude, and GPT-OSS in live production settings, citing a study about AI agents increasing code volume without proportional ticket closure. The framing is heavily stylized and anecdotal, citing a seemingly dramatic statistic from a 'Harvard study' that readers should treat skeptically without verifying the source. There may be some genuine insight into managing AI-generated code review friction, but the style suggests more narrative flourish than rigorous engineering detail.
